text.headline: Three Wars That Shaped the Modern World
text.text: A timeline of key events from the American Civil War (1861–1865), World War I (1914–1918) and World War II (1939–1945).

text.headline: Attack on Fort Sumter
text.text: Confederate forces bombard Fort Sumter in Charleston Harbor, South Carolina, opening the Civil War.

text.headline: Battle of Antietam
text.text: The bloodiest single day in American history ends Lee's first invasion of the North and gives Lincoln the opening to issue the preliminary Emancipation Proclamation.

text.headline: Emancipation Proclamation
text.text: Lincoln declares enslaved people in Confederate-held territory to be free, making abolition a Union war aim.

text.headline: Battle of Gettysburg
text.text: Union victory in Pennsylvania halts Lee's second invasion of the North; Vicksburg falls the next day, splitting the Confederacy.

text.headline: Sherman's March to the Sea
text.text: Union General William T. Sherman marches from Atlanta to Savannah, destroying Confederate infrastructure.

text.headline: Surrender at Appomattox
text.text: Robert E. Lee surrenders the Army of Northern Virginia to Ulysses S. Grant. Lincoln is assassinated five days later.

text.headline: Assassination of Franz Ferdinand
text.text: Archduke Franz Ferdinand of Austria-Hungary is shot in Sarajevo, setting off the July Crisis. War is declared on July 28.

text.headline: First Battle of the Marne
text.text: French and British forces stop the German advance on Paris, leading to years of trench warfare on the Western Front.

text.headline: Battle of the Somme
text.text: One of the deadliest battles in history; the British army suffers about 57,000 casualties on the first day alone.

text.headline: United States Enters the War
text.text: Following unrestricted submarine warfare and the Zimmermann Telegram, the U.S. declares war on Germany.

text.headline: Armistice
text.text: Fighting ends at 11 a.m. on the Western Front. The Treaty of Versailles follows in June 1919.

text.headline: Invasion of Poland
text.text: Germany invades Poland; Britain and France declare war two days later.

text.headline: Battle of Britain
text.text: The Royal Air Force defeats the Luftwaffe's attempt to gain air superiority over Britain.

text.headline: Attack on Pearl Harbor
text.text: Japan attacks the U.S. Pacific Fleet in Hawaii, bringing the United States into the war.

text.headline: Battle of Stalingrad
text.text: The Soviet victory at Stalingrad marks a turning point on the Eastern Front.

text.headline: D-Day
text.text: Allied forces land on the beaches of Normandy, opening a Western Front in Europe.

text.headline: V-E Day
text.text: Germany surrenders unconditionally, ending the war in Europe.

text.headline: Japan Surrenders
text.text: Following the atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki and the Soviet declaration of war, Japan formally surrenders aboard the USS Missouri.
